A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RTTDP study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained content to be matched despite reorganization and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original poisoning evaluations on CIFAR10-C, CIFAR100-C and ImageNet-C, together with method ablations, defense experiments and a budget analysis.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds poisoning baselines, adversarial-attack comparisons, query-count experiments and a distillation-loss comparison.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds a 1/L factor to the summed feature penalties, correcting its displayed loss to match Eq. 6, which already contained this averaging in v1. The surrogate distillation, feature regularization, BLE/NHE objectives and label mapping are retained; an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Both evaluate continual test-time image classification on CIFAR10-C, CIFAR100-C and ImageNet-C at corruption level 5, including uniform and non-uniform poisoning. The new comparisons and ablations use retained datasets and task conditions.

E2.justification: v3 adds Unlearnable Examples and Adversarial Poisoning to the uniform CIFAR10-C/CIFAR100-C comparisons in Tables 2–3. New Tables 8–9 evaluate AutoAttack on CIFAR10-C and ImageNet-C, and GMSA-MIN/GMSA-AVG on CIFAR10-C. MaxCE-PGD matches the existing MaxCE comparator.

E3.justification: New experiments vary PGD steps from 10 to 60 and compare symmetric with forward KLD. The existing budget sweep changes from b = 0.1/0.2/0.5 in v1 A.3.2 to r = 0.1/0.2/0.5 in v3 A.4.4, changing the reported variable from perturbation magnitude to poisoning fraction. Identical table values do not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds two focused ablations: attack effectiveness versus surrogate-query count (Table 10) and symmetric versus forward KLD for distillation (Table 11). Existing component, defense and generalization analyses remain. The old budget analysis is retained numerically but its tested variable is corrected.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without specifying repeated-run counts, random seeds, uncertainty intervals or statistical tests. The additional result tables retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 substantially expands result entries through the new baselines and Tables 8–11. Original benchmark error rates remain, while uniform CIFAR rankings change with comparator membership. A new inconsistency appears: ImageNet-C NHE/CoTTA is 66.40 in v3 Table 9 but 63.84 in both versions’ Table 4; this does not establish a performance gain.

T1.justification: The distribution-matching argument, optimization objectives and label-assignment formulation are retained. Appendix A.1.5 expands the substitutions already used to obtain Eqs. 2–4 into intermediate equations, without adding a new proof, formal bound or substantive mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: realistic grey-box poisoning, feature consistency with BLE/NHE objectives, reassessment of TTA vulnerability and identification of effective defense practices. Changes to the highlighted protocol criteria do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of error propagation through adaptation, surrogate-query costs and the capacity-dependent rationale for symmetric KLD, while acknowledging competitive forward-KLD results. It removes v1’s explicit limitations paragraph concerning grey-box prerequisites and limited gains against strongly defended TTA methods; the grey-box assumption remains elsewhere.

D1.justification: v3 adds code-access information and substantially expands baseline implementation documentation in Appendices A.2–A.3, specifying model initialization, source-model use and explicit attack objectives. The principal 40-step PGD and surrogate-distillation hyperparameters were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v3 adds recent TTA references and literature supporting the newly evaluated poisoning and adversarial-attack methods. Appendices A.1.4 and A.2 elaborate the contrasts with TePA and DIA. The central positioning around relaxing prior attack assumptions remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Section 5 to Section 2. The appendix is substantially reorganized and expanded with explanations of existing optimization steps, protocol differences and comparison implementations. Much main-text prose remains, but the organization and explanatory treatment change substantially.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn and simplified, Tables 2–3 gain comparator rows, and Tables 2–4 explicitly mark adapted methods. Four additional tables and rearranged main-text tables substantially change the presentation. Figures 2–4 remain, and v1’s budget Table 8 becomes v3 Table 12.

improvement.justification: Broader relevant comparisons, focused ablations and clearer implementation documentation provide a limited net improvement in empirical support and reproducibility. These benefits outweigh the removal of the explicit limitations paragraph and the new ImageNet-C NHE/CoTTA inconsistency between Tables 4 and 9, but those shortcomings limit the overall gain.
